learning_outcomes.text: Understand the fundamentals of learning mechanisms specific to neural networks (optimizers, regularization, hyperparameters).
Build neural networks capable of learning to solve classification and regression problems.
Choose the appropriate neural network architecture and loss function in each case, depending on the problem addressed.
Know the most common activation functions and understand their impact on the learning process.
Understand the functioning of convolutional networks and recurrent networks, as well as their applications.
Solve learning tasks using deep neural networks.

syllabus_topics: Modeling non-linear relationships. Non-linear activation functions
Architectures and applications of deep neural networks
Applications: computer vision, natural language processing, etc.
assessment_rules: For the ordinary examination, the final grade is calculated as (0.05 x S) + (0.10 x AO) + 0.45 x ((0.30 x EP1) + (0.70 x EP2)) + (0.40 x ET). A minimum of 4 out of 10 points is required for the practical block (EP1 and EP2 combined) and the theory exam (ET). If these minimums are not met, the final grade will be the minimum between the calculated score and 4. In the extraordinary examination, if a grade of 5 or higher was obtained in either the theoretical or practical part during the ordinary examination, that grade will be maintained. The final grade is calculated as (0.50 x Theory) + (0.50 x Practices), with a minimum of 4 out of 10 required for both the theoretical and practical parts. Otherwise, the final grade will be the minimum between the calculated score and 4. Non-submitted activities count as zero, but if their total weight exceeds 50%, the final grade will be "Not Presented".
